report.verdict: A clean recurring-revenue quarter wrapped in a messy P&L: recurring revenue net of royalties hit a record $7.96m (+9.7% YoY, 99.9% of sales) and Core recurring accelerated to +11.4%, but adj. EBITDA was flat at $3.22m (margin -380bps YoY to 40.4%) on G2E timing and bonus accruals, and the $5.1m / $0.20 GAAP profit is almost entirely the $5.2m Evolution break fee. Deleveraging (2.75x) and a first $1.7m capital return are real; Digital's -4.2% sequential dip on a 31% royalty take, 32% top-two customer concentration into a 2027 contract roll, and a Jan-2028 debt maturity keep this a show-me microcap now that the $3.20 take-out is gone.
summary: **Revenue +8.9% YoY to $7.98m — the fastest growth of 2026** (Q1 -1.6%, Q2 +5.4%, Q3 +8.9%) as the drag from de-emphasised one-time perpetual system sales fades ($12k in Q3 vs $69k). There is no sell-side consensus for this OTCQB name, so the yardstick is the company's own run-rate: recurring revenue net of royalties was a record $7.96m, +9.7% YoY and +1.0% QoQ, and 99.9% of sales.

**Recurring growth is accelerating, led by Core:** recurring revenue YoY went +3.9% (Q1) → +8.5% (Q2) → +9.7% (Q3); Core recurring net of royalties went +3.8% → +7.0% → +11.4%. Digital decelerated the other way (+4.2% → +10.7% → +7.1%) and fell 4.2% sequentially.

**Adj. EBITDA flat at $3.22m (-0.5% YoY, -9.2% QoQ); margin 40.4%, -380bps YoY and -430bps QoQ.** Management attributes ~$0.3m to G2E trade-show costs landing in Q3 (Q4 last year) plus higher incentive-comp accruals against a 'reduced' prior-year accrual. Ex-G2E we estimate ~$3.5m (+9% YoY, ~44% margin) — i.e. in line with revenue growth, so no operating leverage was delivered this quarter despite the 'largely fixed cost base' pitch.

**The GAAP profit is the break fee:** net income $5.13m ($0.20 diluted) vs $1.04m ($0.04) reflects $5.23m of transaction-termination income from Evolution, partly offset by $1.19m of merger-related professional fees (vs $0.31m) and a $0.19m sales/use-tax charge. Income from operations fell 65% to $0.66m. Stripping the fee, merger costs and tax charge, underlying net income was ~$1.28m (our estimate, untaxed), ~12% below the comparable Q3-25 figure.

**No formal guidance; the one outlook change is a softer line on perpetual sales.** FY26 perpetual license sales are now expected to be 'lower' than FY25's $1.18m (Q2 wording: 'slightly lower'); 9M-26 perpetual sales are $0.16m vs $0.83m. Separately, the deck states that partnerships with FanDuel, Caesars, IGT PlayDigital and Delaware North 'have yet to launch product' and are 'expected to produce new revenue in 2027' — nothing in Q4-26.

**The Evolution merger is dead and the $3.20 floor is gone.** Evolution terminated the 18 Jul 2024 merger agreement on 21 Jul 2026 after regulatory approvals failed to arrive (per the 8-K and secondary coverage) and paid the $5,234,678 reverse termination fee in Q3. Secondary sources put the original equity value at ~$85m; at $1.54 the shares sit ~52% below the deal price.

**First-ever capital return, fee-funded:** $4.0m buyback authorised 22 Jul; 330,758 shares repurchased at ~$1.55 ($0.51m, 31 Jul) and all 778,320 Fortress $0.01-strike warrants cancelled for $1.21m (12 Aug, ~$1.56 per warrant). Diluted share count -4.2% (1.11m shares); ~$2.3m remains. Caveat: the BMO First Amendment only permits buybacks funded from the termination fee and requires ≥$5.0m unencumbered liquidity — so this is a one-off pool, not an ongoing programme, unless the lender agrees otherwise.

**Balance sheet:** cash $9.06m (vs $4.8m at Q2-26 and $4.31m at Dec-25); gross term debt $37.69m ($37.37m net of issuance costs, from $39.28m at Dec-25). Net debt ~$28.6m (our calc). Leverage on the company's gross definition 2.75x TTM adj. EBITDA of $13.7m (2.79x Q2-26; 3.22x Q3-25; 4.42x Q4-24); ~2.1x net. Effective interest rate 6.69% vs 7.82% a year ago after the sub-3.0x step-down to SOFR+3.0%.

**Cash flow:** 9M operating cash flow $11.86m including the $5.2m fee (~$6.6m ex-fee, +21% YoY); investing outflow $3.13m (+41%: internally developed software $1.24m, +65%; systems deployed at customer sites $1.41m, +51%); BMO principal repaid $1.94m; $1.73m returned. Q3 FCF (company definition: adj. EBITDA less cash interest, investing and cash taxes) $1.43m, +8.7%; 9M FCF $4.61m, flat YoY; LTM FCF $6.9m = 50% of adj. EBITDA.

**Digital is the quarter's soft spot:** net Digital revenue $3.00m, +7.1% YoY but -4.2% QoQ, on gross revenue flat QoQ (+0.3%) and royalties +12.0% QoQ / +19.5% YoY. The royalty take rose to 31.2% of gross from 28.0% in Q2 and 28.9% a year ago — third-party licensed titles are outgrowing Galaxy-owned content, which dilutes net revenue. Q4-25's record $3.31m Digital quarter is a tough comp.

**Core is the engine:** Core recurring revenue net of royalties $4.96m, +11.4% YoY / +4.4% QoQ, a record, on new U.S. placements and higher participation-based revenue in international markets, driven by the Galaxy Operating System (GOS) progressive platform and the MONOPOLY-branded progressives launched in H1 (named Product Innovation of the Year at the Global Gaming Awards Americas 2026). Progressive-table installs and EZ Baccarat placements are both at records.

**Geography:** EMEA revenue +14.9% YoY to $3.81m (48% of sales; 9M +13.3%); Americas +3.9% to $4.16m (9M -3.0%, reflecting the perpetual-sales wind-down; H1 Americas was -6.2% on our derivation, so Q3 is an inflection). Note all Digital royalty contra-revenue is booked to EMEA.

**Customer concentration is rising, not falling:** two European clients were 18.0% and 14.1% of 9M gross revenue (32% combined; Client B up from 10.6%). The deck identifies Evolution — the jilted acquirer — as the largest Digital customer, and a €6.0m/yr (~$6.8m) minimum-guarantee content agreement (successor to the PGP licence) is in its final contract year to 31 Mar 2027. That renewal is the single biggest 2027 swing factor.

**Cost base ran ahead of revenue:** SG&A +45.6% reported to $5.85m; ex merger costs and the tax charge +21%; ex-G2E as well still ~+12.5% vs +8.9% revenue — incentive comp is the swing (segment note: compensation +19.3% to $2.26m). Stock comp $0.28m vs $0.12m (September option/RSU grants). D&A +11% to $0.90m as capitalised software and deployed systems grow.

**Sales/use-tax clean-up is ongoing:** $0.19m charged in Q3 after $0.51m in Q2 ($0.69m LTM) from self-initiated managed audits and voluntary disclosures across multiple jurisdictions, 'substantially all' pre-2026. BMO's 23 Sep Second Amendment approved a one-time $505,361 covenant EBITDA add-back and lifted the capex cap to 10% of prior-year net revenue — a sign the covenant headroom needed tending.

**Governance and people:** director Meredith Brill stepped down 20 Oct; John M. Boushy appointed Class II director 21 Oct. CTO Anand Singh (ex-Light & Wonder) joined in July. In September the company amended executive employment agreements and granted 270,000 options at $1.656 plus conditional grants of 250,000 restricted shares.

**Product and commercial pipeline:** Galaxy Link all-table linked progressive unveiled at G2E (initial themes MONOPOLY Building Riches and Spotlight Spin in Art Deco); High Card Flush Ultra; Resorts World NYC floor-wide content; MSC Cruises 30 blackjack tables across 7 ships on GOS; Egypt and Germany market entries; Perfect Pairs exclusive global online rights renewed multi-year with Netco. Footprint: 600+ casinos, 30+ countries, 140+ licences, 5,700+ tables; ~3% of U.S. iGaming GGR; 4.5bn+ online wagers a year.

**Refinancing is the next balance-sheet event:** the BMO term loan matures 6 Jan 2028 (the merger-contingent maturity, since the deal did not close by 31 Dec 2025), with $33.75m due in 2028 after $0.56m (Q4-26) and $3.375m (2027) of amortisation. Expect a 2027 refinancing; falling leverage and a 6.7% effective rate help, but the stockholders' deficit is still $(11.5)m.

**Thesis read-through:** at $1.54 (market cap ~$39m; EV ~$67m, our calc) the shares trade on ~4.9x LTM adj. EBITDA and ~9.8x LTM FCF. The 99%-recurring base, 43% LTM margin and 50% FCF conversion are durable; the open questions are Digital's net growth given royalty leakage, the 2027 Evolution contract roll, the 2028 maturity, and whether capital returns continue once the fee-funded $4m is spent.
**Shares -3.8% to $1.54 on the day** (prior close $1.60), on thin OTCQB volume; -41% over twelve months.

segments.name: Core (land-based table games, side bets & progressives)
segments.headline: Record Core recurring revenue of $4.96m (+11.4% YoY) on GOS/MONOPOLY progressive placements; perpetual sales are now a rounding error and the Americas has inflected back to growth.
narrative: They reported Core revenue net of royalties of $4.97m, up 10.0% YoY and 3.5% QoQ, making Core 62% of group revenue. Underneath, recurring license revenue (gross) rose 10.1% to $5.71m, perpetual license sales of progressive gaming systems were just $12k (vs $69k a year ago and $51k in Q2), and royalties netted against gross revenue were essentially flat at $0.75m (13.1% of gross vs 14.0%). The cleanest number — Core recurring revenue net of royalties — reached a record $4.96m, +11.4% YoY and +4.4% QoQ, and the trajectory has clearly accelerated: +3.8% in Q1, +7.0% in Q2, +11.4% in Q3. Management attributed the growth to new game placements in the U.S. and higher participation-based revenue in foreign jurisdictions, 'largely fueled' by the GOS Progressive System and the MONOPOLY-branded progressives rolled out earlier this year; the award of Product Innovation of the Year for the MONOPOLY progressive at the Global Gaming Awards Americas 2026 gives the narrative some external validation.

On volume, the disclosure is thinner than we would like. The last hard datapoint on the installed base was at Q2, when they said recurring-revenue progressive systems were up 11% YoY and 40% versus Q2-24; for Q3 they say only that progressive tables and EZ Baccarat placements both hit records. The footprint is 600+ casinos in 30+ countries, 5,700+ tables carrying Galaxy content and 140+ gaming licences. The commercial model is per billable unit rather than per table — a single table can carry a premium game (or a PRIME enterprise licence), up to three side bets, a progressive and a utility unit, each billed monthly — and management is explicit that the installed base 'sits well below' that multi-unit potential, so growth is meant to come from densifying tables they already serve. There is no disclosure of billable-unit counts, revenue per unit or churn, which makes it impossible to separate price from volume; peers (Light & Wonder, AGS) give table counts and daily yields, and we would push for the same.

The perpetual-sales wind-down is deliberate and now almost complete. One-time system sales were $3.5m in FY24, $1.18m in FY25, $0.83m in 9M-25 and $0.16m in 9M-26; management reiterated that they 'deprioritize' such transactions and now expects FY26 perpetual sales to be 'lower' than FY25 (Q2 said 'slightly lower'). On the deck's LTM framing, one-time hardware sales fell from $1.3m to $0.5m and recurring growth 'more than absorbed' the decline. The geographic consequence is visible: Americas revenue was down 6.2% in H1 (our derivation from the 10-Q 9M and Q3 splits) but up 3.9% in Q3 to $4.16m, so the U.S. placement engine is now outrunning the lost hardware revenue. The remaining comp issue is Q4-25, which carried $0.35m of perpetual sales and will flatter the YoY optics against Q4-26.

The product pipeline shown at G2E is where management wants the conversation: Galaxy Link, an all-table linked progressive that connects every table on the floor to a shared jackpot (launch themes MONOPOLY Building Riches and Spotlight Spin in Art Deco), is pitched as additive billable units on tables already served rather than a swap; High Card Flush Ultra is a new felt variant. Commercial wins include Resorts World NYC (floor-wide content, 'growing further in the fall'), MSC Cruises (30 blackjack tables across seven ships on GOS), Egypt and Germany market entries, and licence applications pending in several new markets. The CEO's line that they 'look forward to converting that interest into placements in the coming quarters' is appropriately hedged by the deck's own caveat that pipeline items are subject to regulatory approval and customer timing; we would not model Galaxy Link revenue before H2-27.

Our judgment is that Core is now the growth engine and the quality of growth is high — recurring, increasingly participation-based internationally, and brand-led — but it is also where the cost went. The ~$0.3m G2E expense that moved into Q3 is a Core selling cost; D&A rose 11% to $0.90m as 9M capex on systems deployed at customer sites rose 51% to $1.41m; and tariffs, which cost $95k in Q3-25, were nil. Cost of ancillary products and assembled components fell 74% to $63k, consistent with fewer hardware sales. The segment carries no separate profit disclosure (the CODM manages on consolidated net income), so Core's margin contribution cannot be verified — a structural limitation of the single-segment reporting.

segments.name: Digital (iGaming content licensing — RNG & live dealer)
segments.headline: Net Digital revenue $3.00m, +7.1% YoY but -4.2% QoQ: gross play was flat sequentially while the royalty take jumped to 31% as licensed third-party titles outgrew owned content.
narrative: They reported Digital revenue net of royalties of $3.00m, up 7.1% YoY but down 4.2% from Q2's $3.14m, with Digital now 38% of group revenue. Gross Digital revenue rose 10.7% YoY to $4.37m but was flat QoQ (+0.3%), while royalties netted against gross revenue rose 19.5% YoY and 12.0% QoQ to $1.37m. The royalty take therefore moved to 31.2% of gross from 28.0% in Q2 and 28.9% in Q3-25 — management says royalties on licensed titles 'increased 20%, growing faster than gross revenue'. Three months earlier they had highlighted the opposite (royalties falling to 28% from 30%), which tells you the owned-versus-licensed mix swings quarter to quarter and that the net line is hostage to which titles happen to be in favour with operators. All Digital revenue is recurring; there are no one-time sales in this stream.

The sequential pattern matters for Q4 modelling: Digital was a record $3.31m in Q4-25 (gross $4.52m), then $2.89m in Q1-26, $3.14m in Q2 and $3.00m in Q3. The deck's framing that Digital is 'growing about 1.6 times as fast as Core' rests on the Q3-24 base (+19% vs +12% over two years); in the current quarter Core (+11.4%) outgrew Digital (+7.1%), and Digital's net growth lags its gross growth by ~360bps because of royalty leakage. The 9M picture is steadier — net +7.4% to $9.03m on gross +9.5%, royalty rate 30.2% vs 28.8% — but the direction of the take rate is the wrong one for net margin.

Market position is described rather than measured: Galaxy content generates roughly 3% of U.S. iGaming GGR, 4.5bn+ wagers a year are placed on Galaxy iGames, and the content is live on 'thousands' of sites via two routes — direct to B2C operators (where Galaxy keeps a larger share) and via B2B aggregators and live-dealer providers. Revenue is a monthly licence per placement plus performance billing as a share of GGR on every wager. They say the 'majority of partners saw amounts played, GGR and royalties improve in Q3 2026' versus Q3-25. There is no disclosure of GGR on content, actives, or per-market growth; the only geographic read-through is EMEA (which carries all Digital royalty contra-revenue) at +14.9% YoY.

Concentration is the issue the deck acknowledges but does not quantify. The 10-Q shows two European clients at 18.0% and 14.1% of 9M gross revenue (vs 19.2% and 10.6%), and the deck names Evolution — which walked away from the acquisition in July — as the largest customer 'under a license agreement'. Separately, the amended-and-restated content agreement inherited from Progressive Games Partners guarantees €6.0m (~$6.8m) per contract year through the year ending 31 Mar 2027, billed at €500k/month minimums; they are now in the final guaranteed year. Deferred revenue under that agreement was €58,576 at 30 Sep 2026 versus €9,637 a year earlier — i.e. billed minimums exceeded usage by more than last year — which is worth watching as the guarantee rolls. Nothing has been said about renewal terms.

The 2027 pipeline is real but entirely prospective: IGT PlayDigital (five-year agreement signed 2025), FanDuel, Caesars and Delaware North/Ruby Seven (social casino) 'have yet to launch product' and are 'expected to produce new revenue in 2027'; Perfect Pairs' exclusive global online rights were renewed multi-year with Netco; EZ Baccarat is being taken online; and internal RNG development is being aligned to land-based titles. Management also leans on expected new U.S. iGaming states, where Galaxy content 'is typically first to market' via its partners. Our take: Digital's economics are attractive (no incremental content cost per market) but net growth in the high single digits, a rising royalty take and a single-customer guarantee expiring in March 2027 argue for modelling net Digital growth at or below gross growth until the new distribution is live.

narrative: Operating costs are where the quarter went wrong. Total costs and expenses rose 34.8% to $7.31m against revenue growth of 8.9%. SG&A was $5.85m, +45.6% YoY; stripping out $1.19m of merger-related professional fees (vs $0.31m) and the $0.19m sales/use-tax charge leaves +20.6%, and removing the ~$0.3m G2E timing effect still leaves ~+12.5%. Geographically, EMEA revenue rose 14.9% YoY to $3.81m (47.8% of group) and the Americas 3.9% to $4.16m; for 9M, EMEA is +13.3% and the Americas -3.0%, with the Americas' H1 decline (-6.2% on our derivation) explained by the perpetual-sales wind-down. The 10-Q allocates all Digital royalty contra-revenue to EMEA, so the regional split understates EMEA gross activity. Currency exposure is euro-denominated (the €6.0m guarantee, European top-two clients); the P&L FX loss was trivial ($1.6k) but the translation adjustment in OCI was $(48)k for the quarter and $(201)k for 9M.

Below the line, interest expense fell 16% to $0.73m (9M -17% to $2.32m) on a lower effective rate (6.69% vs 7.82%) and $2.5m less principal than a year ago; cash interest paid, net, was $0.69m vs $0.84m. The tax provision was $56k on $5.19m of pre-tax income (effective rate ~1%), consistent with NOL utilisation and a deferred tax liability now down to $638. The 9M-25 base included a $2.97m loss on extinguishment of the Fortress debt when the BMO facility was put in place in January 2025, which is why 9M-25 net income was a $32k loss.

The BMO facility — $45.0m term loan plus a $2.0m revolver, Term SOFR + 3.0–3.5% on a leverage grid, interest paid monthly at one-month SOFR — now matures 6 Jan 2028 because the Evolution merger did not complete by 31 Dec 2025. Scheduled maturities are $0.56m (Q4-26), $3.375m (2027) and $33.75m (2028). Covenants cover maximum total funded debt/EBITDA, minimum fixed-charge coverage, minimum EBITDA and maximum capex. Two amendments were signed in the quarter: the First Amendment (24 Jul) permits up to $4.0m of share/warrant repurchases provided they are funded solely from the termination fee, the company retains ≥$5.0m of unencumbered liquid assets and is covenant-compliant, and also reset the fixed-charge coverage definition; the Second Amendment (23 Sep) raised the capex cap to 10% of prior-year net revenue and approved a one-time $505,361 EBITDA add-back (the Q2 sales/use-tax charge) for covenant purposes. Read together, the lender is supportive but is managing headroom carefully.

On the balance sheet, cash of $9.06m against gross debt of $37.69m gives net debt of ~$28.6m (our calc) and net leverage of ~2.1x against the company's 2.75x gross figure. Receivables fell to $4.78m from $5.74m at Dec-25, although unbilled receivables within that rose to $2.59m from $2.09m; accounts payable rose to $2.41m. Total stockholders' deficit narrowed to $(11.5)m from $(17.5)m, almost entirely because of the break fee. The share count is 25.16m after the July repurchase and the August warrant cancellation (1.11m diluted shares removed); the remaining overhang is 1.25m options at a $2.30 weighted strike (713k exercisable) plus the September grants.

highlights.text: Recurring revenue growth is accelerating — +3.9% (Q1) → +8.5% (Q2) → +9.7% (Q3) YoY — to a record $7.96m, now 99.9% of sales; the model has genuinely converted from hardware sales to monthly licence/participation billing.

Core recurring revenue +11.4% YoY / +4.4% QoQ to a record $4.96m on GOS and MONOPOLY-branded progressives (Product Innovation of the Year), with progressive-table and EZ Baccarat installs at records and the Americas back to growth (+3.9%) after an H1 decline.

Interest expense -16% to $0.73m; effective rate 6.69% (from 7.82%); leverage 2.75x gross / ~2.1x net, down from 4.42x at Q4-24; LTM cash interest $2.9m vs $7.0m in FY23 — the refinancing dividend is flowing to FCF.

First capital return: $1.7m deployed to retire 330,758 shares at ~$1.55 and all 778,320 penny warrants at ~$1.56 each, cutting the diluted count 4.2% and removing the Fortress overhang; ~$2.3m of the $4.0m authorisation remains.

Cash $9.06m (up $4.8m YTD) and 9M operating cash flow of $11.9m ($6.6m ex-fee, +21%) funded a 41% step-up in growth capex, $1.9m of debt paydown and the buyback simultaneously; LTM FCF $6.9m = 50% of adj. EBITDA.

2027 distribution pipeline — IGT PlayDigital (5-yr), FanDuel, Caesars, Delaware North social, Perfect Pairs exclusive online renewal — plus Galaxy Link and new-market entries (Egypt, Germany, MSC Cruises, Resorts World NYC) give visible, if unquantified, growth levers beyond the current base.

lowlights.text: Adj. EBITDA flat at $3.22m with margin -380bps YoY / -430bps QoQ to 40.4%; even adding back ~$0.3m of G2E timing, EBITDA grew only in line with revenue (~+9%) because incentive-comp accruals absorbed the operating leverage the deck advertises.

Digital net revenue -4.2% QoQ to $3.00m: gross flat sequentially while royalties jumped 12% QoQ, lifting the royalty take to 31.2% (28.0% in Q2) — licensed titles are outgrowing owned content and net growth (+7.1%) lags gross (+10.7%).

Customer concentration rose: top-two European clients are 32% of 9M gross revenue (18.0% / 14.1%, the latter up from 10.6%); the largest Digital customer is Evolution, the party that just walked from the merger, and the €6.0m/yr minimum-guarantee agreement is in its final contract year to 31 Mar 2027.

SG&A +46% reported and ~+12.5% even after stripping merger fees, the tax charge and G2E, versus +8.9% revenue; stock comp more than doubled after September grants (270k options, 250k conditional RSUs) and amended executive employment agreements.

Sales/use-tax exposure keeps surfacing — $0.19m in Q3 after $0.51m in Q2 ($0.69m LTM) from a self-initiated multi-jurisdiction review that is still 'ongoing'; the lender had to grant a one-time covenant add-back for the Q2 charge.

Buybacks are lender-gated: only termination-fee proceeds may be used, with ≥$5.0m unencumbered liquidity, so capital returns stop at $4.0m absent a further amendment; meanwhile $33.75m of the BMO term loan matures 6 Jan 2028 and must be refinanced in 2027 from a $(11.5)m stockholders'-deficit position.

With the $3.20 Evolution take-out gone, the shares (-3.8% to $1.54 on the day, -41% over 12 months) have no strategic floor, no sell-side coverage and thin OTCQB liquidity; the only outlook change this quarter was a downgrade of FY26 perpetual sales from 'slightly lower' to 'lower'.

forecast.intro: Galaxy does not issue formal revenue or EBITDA guidance, so there is no numeric bridge to reconcile. The qualitative outlook moved in two places: (1) FY26 perpetual license sales of progressive systems are now expected to be 'lower' than FY25's $1.18m (Q2: 'slightly lower'), which is a Core-stream statement and mechanically trims total-revenue growth while leaving recurring revenue untouched; and (2) the deck newly states that the FanDuel, Caesars, IGT PlayDigital and Delaware North partnerships have yet to launch and are expected to produce revenue in 2027, i.e. no Digital contribution in Q4-26. Mechanically, Q4-26 benefits from ~$0.3m of G2E cost that was in Q4-25 and is now in Q3-26, while Q4-25 is a tough top-line comp ($8.24m total including $0.35m perpetual sales and a record $3.31m Digital quarter). Scheduled term-loan amortisation is $0.56m in Q4-26 and $3.375m in 2027; the remaining ~$2.3m buyback capacity is fee-funded and lender-conditioned.

forecast.view: Our Q4-26 estimate is revenue of **$8.3–8.5m** (+1–3% YoY; recurring revenue +4–6% to ~$8.2–8.3m against a $7.89m comp, perpetual sales near zero vs $0.35m) and adj. EBITDA of **$3.7–3.9m** (44–46% margin), giving FY26e revenue of ~$31.9–32.1m (+3–4%) and adj. EBITDA of ~$13.7–13.9m (+3.5–5%) — modest growth masked by the one-time-sales wind-down, with recurring revenue up ~7% for the year. FCF (company definition) should land around **$6.2–6.6m** for FY26 given 9M of $4.6m and a Q4 with no G2E spend but continued elevated growth capex (~$1.0m/quarter). **Leverage should finish the year at ~2.7x gross / ~1.9x net** (our arithmetic: $37.1m gross debt after the December amortisation against TTM adj. EBITDA of ~$13.8m, with cash near $10m absent further buybacks), keeping the SOFR+3.0% grid tier. Margin direction into 2027 is the real debate: the fixed-cost story requires incentive comp and D&A (running +11–19%) to grow slower than the ~7–9% recurring revenue line, and Digital's net margin is being squeezed by a rising royalty take; we would model adj. EBITDA margin flat-to-slightly-up at ~43–44% rather than the expansion the deck implies. The 2027 swing factors are, in order of size, the renewal terms of the €6.0m minimum-guarantee content agreement expiring 31 Mar 2027 (and the broader Evolution relationship post-termination), the timing and scale of the IGT/FanDuel/Caesars/Delaware North launches, the refinancing of the $33.75m 2028 bullet (which, done at current leverage, should be achievable but will consume management bandwidth), and whether the board can secure lender consent to continue buybacks from operating cash once the fee-funded $4.0m is exhausted. Downside risks: further sales/use-tax assessments, a Digital royalty take drifting above 30% structurally, and any slippage in Galaxy Link placements. Upside: Core recurring sustaining double-digit growth on MONOPOLY/Galaxy Link densification and a 2027 Digital step-up from new distribution.
